panels.heading: No owner?
panels.support: Name the person who will own it.

notes: At a quarterly, put the current Function Chart on the screen. Ask where ownership was unclear last quarter, then fix the chart.
Restate the rule: every function has one accountable owner. One person is accountable for the work. Others may be responsible to contribute to the work.
In private mode, each person writes who holds each function; reveal, then agree. Resolve differences about current accountability. Add any new or planned functions.
Finish when every function has one owner who said yes out loud.
Allow about 25 minutes, with the Team View after it.
Open the Team View in Metronome on the screen. Fix any difference from the chart now.
When one person owns two functions, it shows in red: a load to watch. Planned functions show where people can grow.
Each owner says their critical number out loud. It answers one question: did I have a good day? A person who owns two functions names one for each.
Show the Team View to the whole team at a town hall whenever it changes.

override.support: In Metronome: open Scorecards. The Head of Company goes first.
body: Head of Company: walk the team through yours.
Each leader: where does yours stand?
notes: At a quarterly, this is a check-in. Open the Head of Company scorecard in Metronome, and the Head of Company walks the team through it.
Then ask each leader where their own scorecard stands.

A scorecard is one page for a function. It says what success looks like: a purpose in one sentence, three to five functional accountabilities, each starting Owns, exactly two metrics, six to eight key competencies, and the company's core values. The two metrics are one widget the owner controls and one fiscal metric the role owns.
The company's Core Values go on every scorecard. If the team has agreed them, check they are there. If not, they go on once the team agrees them.
Scorecards are reviewed every 90 days. The scores: 0 below, 1 meets, 2 exceeds. The owner scores first, then their team lead, then they talk about the differences.
Homework: every leader completes their function scorecard in Metronome, and builds one for each direct report.

override.title: Are you pushing all six levers?
override.headline: Are you pushing all six levers?
notes: At a quarterly, the six levers are the check on the KFFM. The map is only right if the team is using it to move more cash faster.
The levers are quantity, conversion, price, timing, capacity and cost. They are the ways the owner manages cash.
Timing is how long one widget takes to get through. Capacity is how many widgets a function can handle in a month. A function can be fast and still too small.
Use the example to name each lever. Then go to the team's own KFFM on the next slide.
